subject: lavaan makes my R crash :( (Windows users only)

messages.author: 373e56ec89625c50
messages.subject: lavaan makes my R crash :( (Windows users only)
parts:
hello there. I have been going nuts lately with an error in R that is some unholy combination of something wrong with lavaan AND I think my computer (or some other computers). I have tried everything: running the latest version of R, downgrading R, upgrading lavaan, downgrading lavaan, everything and I can't seem to get rid of it.

the problem is that this only happens in Windows (so iOs and Linux users are safe), only happens when asking lavaan to do something that takes a long time (like a simulation or fitting some complicated model by WLS) and although it happens often, it doesn't happen all the time.

after it runs lavaan for a while, it gives me the following error:

"R for Windows GUI front-end has stopped working

A problem caused the program to stop working correctly. Windows will close the program and notify you if a solution is available "

and shuts down R. I lose all control of R at that moment so there isn't anything within R I can do to try and see what the error is. after hours of googling this error I can see that other people have experienced it, I can see that it happens to some (but not all computers) and that is some perfect storm of something wrong with lavaan and with the users computer.

I was trying to use the tryCatch() function to see what it will do, but a much more experienced R user (and friend of mine) told me that:

"It's a decent idea but I doubt it will work. tryCatch will catch errors thrown in the code itself but those types of errors don't actually crash R. My guess is that there is some sort of error in some compiled code that lavaan is running which causes a serious error that R can't recover from and that tryCatch won't be able to catch at all"

here's a sample code that produces the error. notice that all it does is generate data and take the mean. if you try the code over and over and over again, eventually it will finish... but it's frustrating to try and run simulations over and over again, knowing that at any moment R might crash and everything you have will get lost! :(

library(lavaan)

mod1 <- '   nu1 =~ 0.7*y1 +0.7*y2 +0.7*y3
                  nu2 =~ 0.7*y4 +0.7*y5 +0.7*y6
                  nu3 =~ 0.7*y7 +0.7*y8 +0.7*y9
        
         nu1 ~~ 0.3*nu3
         nu1 ~~ 0.3*nu2
         nu2 ~~ 0.3*nu3
         
  y1 ~~ 0.51*y1
  y2 ~~ 0.51*y2
  y3 ~~ 0.51*y3
  y4 ~~ 0.51*y4
  y5 ~~ 0.51*y5
  y6 ~~ 0.51*y6
  y7 ~~ 0.51*y7
  y8 ~~ 0.51*y8
  y9 ~~ 0.51*y9
  '

reps <- 1000

y1k <- double(reps)

for (i in 1:reps) {

datum1 <- simulateData(mod1, sample.nobs=500, skewness=c(rep(3,9)), kurtosis=c(rep(21,9)))

y1k[i] <- mean(datum1)

}

On 03/20/2014 05:48 PM, Oscar Olvera wrote:
> *sigh* oh well... it's probably just me then. i'll still leave this
> thread open just in case anyone else happens to stumble upon this error.

Oscar,

Please understand this: lavaan (0.5-16) is written in 100% R. Therefore,
lavaan -on its own- is unable to crash your system, even if we would try
very hard. I am afraid the title of your post is a bit misleading.

So, if you experience a crash, and software is the cause, you should
blame R. Are you using vanilla R? (Or a revolution or other flavor).
Which version? Custom compiled? Perhaps against third-party blas/lapack
libraries? And most importantly, do yo see any type of message (a stack
trace)? If so, can you show it to us? Or does your machine freeze? In
that case, it is a hardware issue.

My guess would be that this is a memory related issue. In your script,
make sure that you remove unused matrices/containers, and run the
garbage collecter -gc()- afterwards. You can also use Rprofmem() to
monitor memory use in an R session.

Hope this helps,

Yves.
